concept.name: Effective leverage
concept.definition: The ratio of a portfolio's total position exposure to its equity — typically gross exposure divided by net asset value — expressing how many dollars of market exposure are controlled per dollar of capital.
concept.intuition: It is the real multiplier on your capital: effective leverage of 3x means a 10% adverse market move costs about 30% of equity, before hedging effects.
concept.mechanics: Sum absolute position values (or notionals for derivatives) and divide by account equity; for a single margined position it approximates position notional divided by margin posted. It changes dynamically as prices move and as equity or margin balances fluctuate.
concept.formula: Effective leverage = gross exposure / equity = (|longs| + |shorts|) / NAV; for one margined position, approximately position notional / margin posted.
concept.failure_modes: Gross-based effective leverage ignores netting and correlation, overstating risk for hedged books, while notional-based versions understate risk for convex instruments such as options, whose delta-adjusted exposure moves. It also spikes passively when equity falls, tightening margin pressure in downturns.
concept.misconceptions: An account's leverage setting (e.g. 10x) is a cap, not the leverage actually in use: effective leverage is what the open positions imply at a given moment, and it drifts with every price tick.
concept.example: $200,000 of positions on $50,000 of equity is 4x effective leverage; a 5% adverse move then costs roughly $10,000, or 20% of equity.
